chunks: And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to begin with the takbīr when he prayed the ẓuhr prayer on the Day of Naḥr, and he would stop the takbīr on the last of the Days of Tashrīq at dawn. He would recite the takbīr after every salat (prayer), saying: “Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise.”

When he reached the prayer ground, he stepped forward and led the people in salat (prayer) without an adhān or iqāmah. When he finished the salat (prayer), he ascended the minbar and began, saying: “Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, equal to the weight of His Throne, the pleasure of His Self, and the number of the drops of His sky and His seas. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names, and praise belongs to Allah until He is pleased, and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving. Allah is the Greatest, supremely great, exalted in majesty, and a God mighty in honor, merciful and tender; He pardons despite having power, and none despairs of His mercy except the misguided. Allah is the Greatest, greatly; there is no god but Allah abundantly; and glory be to Allah, ever-compassionate, all-powerful. Praise belongs to Allah: we praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, seek His guidance, and bear witness that there is no god but He, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided and attained a mighty success; and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly gone far astray and suffered a manifest loss.”

I counsel you, servants of Allah, to have taqwā of Allah, to remember death often, and to renounce this world, which those before you did not truly enjoy and which will not remain for anyone after you. Your course in it is the course of those who have passed: do you not see that it has worn away, announced its passing, its familiar good has become strange, and it has turned away swiftly? It announces annihilation, and its inhabitant is driven on toward death. Its sweetness has turned bitter, its clarity has become turbid, and nothing remains of it except a remnant like the little left in a waterskin and a sip like the sip left in a vessel, which the thirsty one sips yet it does not quench his thirst. So resolve, servants of Allah, to depart from this abode, whose people are decreed to perish, prevented from lasting life, and humbled by death. No living one can hope to remain, and no soul but is resigned to death. So let not hope overcome you, nor the long span delude you, nor be deceived in it by false hopes; rather, worship Allah in the days of life.

By Allah, if you were to wail like the grieving, bereft one in haste, supplicate like mankind supplicates, cry out like the devoted cries of monks, and leave behind wealth and children seeking nearness to Him for a raised rank with Him or the forgiveness of a sin recorded by His scribes and preserved by His messengers, it would still be little compared with what I hope for you of His reward and what I fear for you of His painful punishment. By Allah, if your hearts were to melt away and your eyes were to flow with blood out of longing for Him and fear of Him, then you lived in the world for as long as the world remained, your deeds would still not repay His mighty blessings upon you and His guiding you to faith. You would never deserve, by your deeds, His Garden or His mercy; rather, by His mercy you are shown mercy, by His guidance you are guided, and by them you come to His Garden. May Allah make us and you among the repentant worshippers.

Indeed this is a day whose sanctity is immense, whose blessing is hoped for, and in which forgiveness is expected. So increase the remembrance of Allah Most High, seek His forgiveness, and repent to Him: indeed, He is the Oft-Returning, the Merciful. Whoever among you offers as sacrifice a young goat, it does not suffice for him, but a young sheep does suffice. Among the completeness of the sacrifice is inspection of its eye and ear; if the eye and ear are sound, the sacrifice is complete. But if it has a broken horn, or drags its legs to the place of sacrifice, it does not suffice. When you offer sacrifice, then eat, feed others, give gifts, and praise Allah for what He has provided you of grazing livestock. And establish salat (prayer), give zakat, excel in worship, uphold the testimony, and desire what He has prescribed and obligated upon you of jihad, hajj, and fasting; for the reward of that is immense and does not end, and abandoning it is a consequence that does not perish.

Enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, intimidate the oppressor, support the oppressed, restrain the suspect one, deal well with women and those whom your right hands possess, speak truthfully, render trusts, and stand firmly for the truth. And let not the life of this world delude you, nor let the Deluder delude you concerning Allah. Indeed, the best speech is the remembrance of Allah, and the most eloquent admonition for the Godwary is the Book of Allah.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begot nor was begotten. And there is none comparable to Him.”
And he would recite: “Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn” to its end, or “Alhākumu al-takāthur” to its end, or “Wa al-ʿaṣr.”

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام recite and teach in the Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer and sermon?
ai.summary: This report describes the practice of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in the Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer, the takbīrāt following the prayers of the Days of Tashrīq, and a long sermon combining praise of Allah, exhortation toward taqwā, remembrance of death, repentance, and legal guidance regarding sacrifice and religious duties. It joins devotional practice, ethical counsel, and jurisprudential rulings, while emphasizing that salvation and entry into Paradise are by Allah’s mercy and guidance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1484 – Imam Ali (as), used to begin with the Takbir when he prayed the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Eid al-Nahr (Eid al-Adha), and he would cease the Takbir on the last day of the Tashriq (the days after Eid) at dawn. He would say the Takbir after every prayer, saying:
"Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, and to Allah (swt) belongs the praise."
When he reached the prayer ground, he would step forward and lead the people in prayer without an Adhan (call to prayer) or Iqamah (second call to prayer). When he finished the prayer, he would ascend the pulpit and begin by saying:
"Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, equal to the weight of His Throne, the pleasure of His Self, the amount of the drops in His sky and His seas. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. Praise be to Allah (swt) until He is pleased, and He is the Almighty, the Most Forgiving. Allah (swt) is the Greatest, the Grandest in greatness, a God of majesty and mercy, forgiving even after possessing power, and none despairs of His mercy except the misguided ones."
"Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Great beyond measure, and there is no god but Allah (swt) in abundance. Glory be to Allah (swt), the Most Kind and the All-Powerful. Praise be to Allah (swt); we praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, and seek His guidance. We bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt) alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger."
"Whoever obeys Allah (swt) and His Messenger has indeed been guided and achieved a great success. And whoever disobeys Allah (swt) and His Messenger has indeed gone astray in a distant misguidance and incurred a manifest loss."
"I advise you, O’ servants of Allah (swt), to be conscious of Allah (swt), to frequently remember death, and to live a life of detachment from this world, which those before you who inhabited it could not hold onto, and which will not remain for anyone after you. Your path in this world is the same as those who have passed before you. Do you not see that it has already ended, that it has given signs of its impending disappearance, that its known blessings have turned strange, and that it has turned its back and is departing?"
"This world has warned of its end, and its residents are pushed toward death. What was once sweet has turned bitter, and what was once clear has become murky. Nothing remains of it except a remnant, like the remnants left in a container, a mouthful to quench the thirst of the parched, but it does not satisfy them."
"So, O’ servants of Allah (swt), prepare to depart from this abode. It is destined for its inhabitants to pass away, it denies them the comforts of life, and it humiliates them with death. No living soul has hope for permanence, and no soul has an escape from death."
"Do not let long hopes overpower you, and do not let the passage of time deceive you. Do not be deceived by hopes in this world. Worship Allah (swt) during your lifetime. 
By Allah (swt), even if you were to wail like a lost and grieving mother, call out to Allah (swt) as if from the depths of your soul, weep like monks devoted to solitude, give up your wealth and children seeking closeness to Him, striving for a high rank in His sight or the forgiveness of a sin noted by His scribes and preserved by His messengers, all this would be small in what I hope for you from His reward and what I fear for you from His painful punishment."
"By Allah (swt), even if your hearts melted and your eyes wept from yearning for Him and fear of Him, even if you lived in this world as long as it remains, your actions would not be enough to earn His Paradise or His mercy, but by His mercy, you are shown mercy, and by His guidance, you are guided, and by them, you reach His Paradise."
"May Allah (swt) make us and you among the repentant and the worshipful. 
Indeed, this day is a day of great sanctity, a day of expected blessings, and a day in which forgiveness is hoped for. So, remember Allah (swt) abundantly, seek His forgiveness, and turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful."
"And whoever among you sacrifices a young goat, it will not suffice for him, but a young sheep will suffice. For the completion of the sacrifice, look for sound eyes and ears. If the eyes and ears are sound, the sacrifice is complete. However, if it has a broken horn or drags its legs, it will not suffice. When you make the sacrifice, eat, feed others, and give as gifts. And praise Allah (swt) for providing you with cattle from livestock."
"Establish the prayer, give zakat, worship Allah (swt) sincerely, bear witness to the truth, and yearn for what He has prescribed and obligated upon you in striving, pilgrimage, and fasting, for the reward of these is great and everlasting, while neglecting them results in eternal misfortune and ruin."
"Enjoin what is good, forbid what is evil, frighten the oppressor, support the oppressed, restrain the transgressor, be kind to women and those under your care, speak the truth, fulfil your trusts, uphold justice, and do not let the worldly life deceive you, nor let the deceiver deceive you about Allah (swt)."
"Indeed, the best speech is the remembrance of Allah (swt), and the most eloquent advice for the God-conscious is the Book of Allah (swt)."
"I seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the accursed devil. In the name of Allah (swt), the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say: 'He is Allah (swt), the One. Allah (swt), the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is begotten. And there is none comparable to Him.'"
Then he would recite either "Say, O’ disbelievers" to its end, or "The mutual rivalry for piling up of worldly things diverts you" to its end, or "By time."
